A molecular clock of accumulated EAE damage

RRMAP2 spinal-cord Xenium · relapsing–remitting cohort · 33 animals · 5101-gene panel · animal-level pseudobulk. A supervised clock that reads disease duration from tissue — the cumulative, irreversible axis that grows with disease history, after current severity is removed.

Headline. EAE tissue carries two separable molecular clocks. Severity is acute and reversible — it resets at each relapse. Duration is cumulative and irreversible. A multivariate elastic-net clock predicts time-since-induction at Spearman +0.80 (leave-one-animal-out) even after severity is removed (permutation p = 0.020), and it strengthens — not weakens — when sex and cord region are additionally controlled (+0.86). The signature reads as the biology of an aging lesion field: neuron/myelin loss, a basement-membrane→fibrotic-scar switch, lymphoid organization, and a lipid synthesis→scavenging switch. A model-free pass over the relapse cycle recovers the same split independently — genes that oscillate with each attack and reset (severity) versus genes whose remission floor ratchets upward (duration).

The big idea

The setting. EAE is the mouse model of multiple sclerosis: an autoimmune attack on the spinal cord. It comes in two courses — relapsing–remitting (attacks that flare and recede) and chronic-progressive (sustained worsening) — the same two courses seen in human MS. We profile spinal-cord tissue with spatial transcriptomics (Xenium, 5,101 genes) and ask what the tissue records about the disease.

The problem. Each mouse is sampled once, and given a clinical score for how sick it is at that moment. That score sees current disease activity but is largely blind to the damage piled up from earlier attacks. Two mice can look equally sick yet be at very different points in their disease history.

The central claim. Tissue carries two separable molecular clocks. Severity is acute and reversible — it rises in an attack and resets in remission. Duration is cumulative and irreversible — it grows with how long disease has run, regardless of how sick the animal looks today. Most of this report is about measuring the second one cleanly, separating it from the first and from technical confounds.

The answer. A molecular clock reads disease duration from tissue at Spearman +0.80 after severity is removed; it is not a sex/region/batch artifact; the accruing program is a glia-led, per-cell shift; and it replicates in a second EAE model and strain.

How to read this — our approach

Five ideas that recur1 · The animal is the unit. Cells within one mouse aren't independent, so every model is trained and tested with whole animals held out (no cell from a test animal is ever seen in training).
2 · Pseudobulk. We average each animal's cells into one expression profile per gene — a stable, animal-level summary.
3 · Removing severity (“orthogonalization”). To ask what tracks duration and not just sickness, we statistically subtract the clinical score from both the genes and the time label first — so nothing can score well just by reading how sick the animal is.
4 · A clock. A regression that predicts time-since-induction from the de-severitied expression. Good prediction on held-out animals = the tissue genuinely tracks duration.
5 · Shuffle test. We scramble the time labels and refit many times; if the real clock beats every shuffle, it isn't an accident of a small cohort.

Exact estimators, parameters and tests are in Methods at the end. The findings below build in four steps: I the two behaviours in the raw data, II a clock that reads duration, III what that clock is actually reading, and IV whether it generalizes and what it means for disease course.

Part I
Two clocks in one tissue
The ideaBefore any model: do genes actually behave in two different ways over the relapse cycle? Yes. Some flare with every attack and snap back to baseline in remission — the reversible severity axis. Others never fully come back down; their baseline creeps up attack after attack — the irreversible duration axis. This single distinction is the backbone of everything that follows.

Two behaviours along the relapse cycle

Start with the simplest, model-free view. Track each gene across the relapse cycle CFA→ONSET→PEAK1→REM1→PEAK2→REM2→PEAK3 and two distinct behaviours fall out: genes that spike at every attack and reset in remission, and genes whose remission floor ratchets upward cycle after cycle.

Two measurable behaviours. amplitude (peak − remission) measures how hard a gene oscillates with each attack; floor_drift (REMISSION2 − REMISSION1) measures whether it stays elevated after the animal has clinically recovered. 149 genes are acute oscillators (spike, then reset), 79 ratchet upward (survive remission). These are the two raw faces of the severity axis (oscillates, reversible) and the duration axis (accumulates, irreversible) — everything that follows makes the second one quantitative.

Part II
A clock that reads disease duration
The ideaNow we make the duration axis quantitative. We train a model to predict how long disease has run from tissue — with current severity statistically removed — and then spend three sections trying to break it: a shuffle test, and checks that it isn't secretly reading sex, cord region, or batch.

The clock predicts duration beyond severity

Each dot is one held-out animal: its predicted duration-residual vs the truth. The points hug the diagonal across all three cord regions.

Clock B (severity-orthogonalized): LOAO Spearman +0.80, R² +0.67. Genes and day are residualized on the clinical score within each training fold, so the clock cannot cheat through severity. For contrast, predicting day from severity alone gives -0.52 — negative: later timepoints are not sicker, the relapse cycle resets acute severity. That decoupling is what makes duration identifiable. A cross-target control (predict score from day-residualized features) gives +0.84, confirming the transcriptome carries both axes separably.

Validation — the clock beats a shuffled null

Could a clock this good arise by chance from 33 animals? We shuffle the day labels and refit, 50 times. None of the shuffles come close.

Permutation null mean ρ = -0.07; observed +0.80; p = 0.0196 (floor for 50 permutations). The clock is not an over-fit. Day-of-sacrifice is also clean of technical batch within RR: Kruskal p(day) = 0.1379 (run_date), 0.7168 (animal multiplex), 0.2145 (region).

The clock is not a sex, region or severity artifact

Two nuisance axes could masquerade as time: sex (the signature includes the X-marker Xist) and cord region. Removing them makes the clock stronger, not weaker.

Fully-controlled clock (severity + sex + region, Xist dropped): Spearman +0.86, R² +0.73 — above the original +0.80. Sex is orthogonal to day (Xist-raw vs day ρ = -0.05; Mann-Whitney day~sex p = 0.1768), and region tracks severity more than time (see below). Removing these nuisance directions sharpens the temporal signal.

Region — a spatial gradient that aligns with severity

EAE has a spatial cord gradient. It is real, but it indexes how severe the tissue is, not how long disease has run — so it cannot be what the clock reads.

Cervical carries the most severe disease here (mean score C = 1.77 > T = 1.31 > L = 1.00); lumbar is sampled earliest. Region orders with severity (ordinal L<T<C vs score ρ = +0.28) but is not significantly tied to day (Kruskal p = 0.2145; ordinal vs day ρ = +0.18, p = 0.329). Because clock B already removes severity, the region gradient cannot drive it — confirmed by the fully-controlled clock above.

Part III
What the clock is reading
The ideaThe clock works — so what is it actually keying on? Four questions: which genes carry the duration signal (vs the severity one), is the rise real per-cell upregulation or just more cells, what is the biology of the accruing program, and where in the tissue does it live.

Which genes carry each clock — day vs severity

The clock above is multivariate. This asks the same question one gene at a time, on the same continuous axis the clock regresses on: for every gene we take its partial correlation with day-of-sacrifice with severity removed (the accrual / duration axis) and with severity with day removed (the oscillation / severity axis). day and severity are near-orthogonal across animals (r = +0.17), so a gene can load on either, both, or neither.

The gene-level decomposition reproduces the clock and splits its biology cleanly. Of 5101 genes, 1076 accrue with day and 786 decline (severity removed; 909 at day-FDR q<0.05), while 2115 track severity but are flat on day — they oscillate with the relapse and reset. The day-partial correlations line up with the supervised clock coefficients (Spearman +0.60, sign-agreement 81% over 135 clock genes), so the clock's weights are reading real per-gene temporal trends, not multivariate artifacts. The declining arm is dominated by the interferon program (Stat2, Usp18, Irgm1, Isg15, Oasl2) — acute and severity-linked, exactly the genes the clock sees receding with duration.

Is the accrual real upregulation, or just more cells?

A pseudobulk gene can rise with duration for two very different reasons: the cell type that makes it becomes more abundant (compositional — TLS B/T cells, foamy macrophages, fibroblast-like cells) or each cell makes more of it (cell-intrinsic). Using per-(animal × cell-type) means and cell counts, we split every accruing gene's severity-removed day trend into the two — a shift-share decomposition that the animal-level clock cannot do on its own.

The accrual is overwhelmingly cell-intrinsic, not compositional. Across 1260 accruing genes the median day trend is 90% per-cell upregulation vs only 11% cell-number; of the 825 strongly-accruing genes, 806 are intrinsic-driven and just 2 compositional (17 mixed). In the right panel almost every gene sits far below the diagonal (intrinsic ≫ compositional). The duration clock is reading a genuine shift in cell state, which matches the localization result that a clock built on cell-type proportions alone is far weaker than one on expression.
The cell counts make the point sharper, not weaker. With severity removed, the compartments that expand with duration are astrocyte (+0.45), vascular/endo (+0.38), microglia (+0.27) — gliosis and vascular/fibrotic scar — while the inflammatory compartments shrink (T/NK (-0.42), infl-myeloid (-0.35), oligo/myelin (-0.14)). Yet the foamy / scavenger-macrophage program (Mrc1, Folr2, Cd68, Ctsk, Atp6v0d2) still accrues strongly — so it is myeloid cells changing state (becoming foamy/lipid-laden) as their numbers fall, not an influx of new ones. The few compositional genes track the expanding astrocyte and vascular compartments.

The biology — an aging lesion field

The multivariate clock picks non-redundant genes, so it reads as a coherent six-part chronic-progression program (↑ accrues with duration, ↓ declines; severity removed).

moduledirectiongenes
Neurodegeneration / demyelination↓ declinesMog, Mal, Uchl1, Syn1, Nptx2, Gad1, Gad2, Slc17a6
Acute innate / interferon↓ recedesCcr2, Tmem173/STING, Ifit1, Ifit3, Irf5, H2-D1, Tmem119, Siglech
Basement-membrane → fibrotic scar↓ Col4a1/2, Eln · ↑ scarThbs2↑, Serpine2↑, Ptx3↑, Fbln2↑, Hpse↑, Klf5↑
Adaptive / lymphoid organization↑ follicular · ↓ plasmaCxcl13↑, Cxcl12↑, Tcf7↑, Il2ra↑ · Mzb1↓, Jchain↓
Lipid: synthesis → scavenging↓ synth · ↑ uptakeHmgcr↓, Idi1↓, Msmo1↓, Ldlr↓ · Lpl↑, Pltp↑, Abca8a↑, Srebf1↑
Circadian / gliotic repair↑ accruesNr1d1, Dbp, Bhlhe40, Per1 · Igf1, Igfbp2, Il33, S1pr3
Circadian genes are real, not a sampling artifact. Sacrifice time-of-day is constant across animals, so Nr1d1/Dbp/Bhlhe40/Per1 reflect a genuine shift in circadian/metabolic regulation with disease duration.

Where the clock lives — spatial localization

The clock says tissue tracks duration; this asks which cell types and niches carry it. We rebuild the same severity-orthogonalized clock independently inside each compartment (too few animals for a black-box attention net) and rank by held-out accuracy.

Duration is a tissue-wide chronic program that peaks in glia. Every compartment carries it (LOAO ρ +0.69 to +0.89), led by astrocyte (ρ +0.89, perm p=0.0196), oligo/myelin and myeloid — neurons and lymphocytes carry the least. Crucially, a clock built on cell-type proportions alone is far weaker (composition ρ +0.52, perm p=0.0392): the signal is cells changing state, not just shifting in number. The strongest spatial niche is niche3 (vascular/endo) (ρ +0.84, perm p=0.0196).

Each gene module sits in its expected cell type

The clock-gene modules are not diffuse — they map onto the cell types that produce them, which is what makes the tissue-wide signal mechanistically interpretable.

Lymphoid genes (Cxcl13, Mzb1, Jchain) in B/plasma; scar/matricellular (Thbs2, Ptx3, Serpine2) in astrocytes; basement-membrane (Col4a1/2, Eln, Cxcl12) in vascular/endothelial; myelin (Mog, Mal) in oligodendrocytes; foamy-lipid uptake (Lpl) in myeloid; cholesterol synthesis (Hmgcr, Idi1, Msmo1) in OPC/oligo; neuronal (Uchl1, Gad1, Slc17a6) in neurons.

Part IV
Does it generalize, and what does it mean?
The ideaTwo payoff questions. Generality: is this duration program specific to one model, or a shared feature of CNS autoimmune damage — does it replicate in a second EAE model and strain? Meaning: what separates an animal that relapses from one that doesn't — the disease-course question the whole project circles.

Cross-model — the clock replicates in the chronic arm

The duration clock was built on RR because chronic day-of-sacrifice was thought to alias batch. The corrected metadata shows otherwise: chronic has a continuous day axis (8–50 dpi) that is clean of run_date, so we can run the identical clock there and ask whether the duration program is the same across two models and two strains (RR = SJL/PLP, chronic = B6/MOG).

The duration clock is not RR-specific. Rebuilt identically on the chronic arm it reaches Spearman +0.86 (R² +0.86, permutation p = 0.020, 128 genes), with day clean of batch (Kruskal day~run_date p = 0.57). And the two duration axes agree: the per-gene RR day-trend correlates with the chronic day-trend at Spearman +0.65 (5101 genes, 72% sign-agreement) — across both strain and model. The agreement is specific to the duration axis: the RR severity-oscillation axis does not transfer to chronic duration (Spearman -0.17).
One revealing difference. In chronic, predicting day from severity alone is positive (Spearman +0.52) — the disease is monotonically progressive, so later really is sicker. In RR the same baseline is negative (-0.52) because each relapse resets acute severity. Same accruing program underneath; opposite severity–time coupling on top — which is exactly the distinction between a relapsing and a progressive course.

Within-strain — what predisposes to relapse?

Exploratory, n = 5 / 4 / 4. Conserved duration does not mean there are no relapse-specific markers — and the cross-model contrast can't address course (RR vs chronic is strain-confounded). The identifiable cut is within SJL/PLP. By design REMISSION1 (~day 22) branches into MONOPHASIC (~day 33, did not relapse) and PEAK2 (~day 32, relapsed): monophasic animals are sampled at the same timepoint a relapser hits its second attack (day MW p = 0.16) but stay low-severity (0.62 vs 2.44). So the time-matched contrast is MONO vs PEAK2, and the relapse decision is the divergence of the two trajectories from the shared REM1 origin. Cross-sectional (different animals; we cannot label a REM1 animal's future), n tiny — effect sizes and direction only.
Relapse re-ignites the acute program; not-relapsing resolves and keeps accruing quietly. From the REM1 origin, the relapse path (→PEAK2) turns the acute-oscillator module back on (z -0.21→+0.42), with innate/IFN and ECM/scar, and loses neuron/myelin again (-0.07→-0.30). The monophasic path (→MONO) does the opposite: the acute oscillator stays off (-0.53), neuron/myelin recovers (→+0.33), the glucocorticoid/stress tone resolves (+0.30→-0.56), and the quiet duration/repair accrual continues — the monophasic-specific genes are the conserved accrual set Igf2, Fmod, Vtn plus circadian Nr1d1. The relapse-specific genes are the acute myeloid/oscillator program (Gpnmb, Chil1, Arg1, Timp1, Hal, Socs3).

The relapse-specific direction (PEAK2 − MONO) aligns with the acute severity/oscillation axis (Spearman +0.85 vs oscillation amplitude, +0.84 vs the score-axis) and runs opposite the duration axis (-0.56). So relapse = re-running the acute attack program; staying monophasic = resolving it and continuing the slow accrual/repair trajectory.

Honest reading. PEAK2 is a severity peak by construction, so “relapse-specific” genes are expected to be the acute severity program — the informative half is the monophasic trajectory (myelin recovery + stress resolution + quiet accrual). And because the data are terminal/cross-sectional, this is a population-level trajectory, not proof that anything at REM1 decides the outcome; that would need a longitudinal or pre-relapse design. Full table: runs/monophasic_vs_relapsing/rem1_trajectory_genes.csv. Source: scripts/monophasic_vs_relapsing.py.

Part Ref
Methods, limits & next steps

Methods — data, models, and statistics

Everything in this report is built from animal-level pseudobulk and cached per-cell-type aggregates; no analysis below re-reads the raw cell-by-gene matrix. Each section names the script that produces it.

Data & cohort

RRMAP2 spinal-cord Xenium, a targeted 5101-gene panel. The headline clock is the relapsing–remitting cohort (33 animals, SJL/PLP); the chronic arm (34 animals, B6/MOG) is analysed separately for cross-model replication. With corrected metadata the chronic day_of_sacrifice is continuous (8–50 dpi) and clean of run_date (Kruskal p≈0.57) — the earlier batch-alias concern was an artifact of the coarse day16/day30 stage grouping, not the underlying day. Each animal is a single terminal timepoint (cross-sectional — no within-animal time courses), labelled with day_of_sacrifice (11–49 days post-induction) and a clinical score_sacrifice. Pseudobulk = per-animal mean of log CP10k over all cells (runs/rr_within_relapse/pseudobulk.npz); per-(animal × leiden-cluster × gene) means and cell counts come from runs/rr_phase_niche/agg_leiden_1.npz.

The duration clock (supervised regression)

Elastic-net (ElasticNetCV, l1-ratio 0.5, 5-fold inner CV, 50-alpha path, features standardized) under leave-one-animal-out outer CV; accuracy is Spearman ρ and R² on the held-out predictions. A per-fold top-1000-variance prefilter (computed on the training fold only — no leakage) cuts 5101→1000 features. Clock A regresses day on genes directly. Clock B (headline) is severity-orthogonalized: within every training fold both the gene matrix and day are linearly residualized on score_sacrifice, so the clock predicts the part of duration that severity cannot explain; the evaluation target is the full-data day-residual. The signature is the nonzero coefficients of a full-data Clock-B fit. Source: scripts/duration_clock.py.

Adversarial controls. (i) severity-only baseline — predict day from score alone; (ii) cross-target — run the same pipeline predicting score from day-residualized features (axes separable?); (iii) permutation null — shuffle day across animals and refit Clock B 50×, p = (1 + #{ρperm ≥ ρobs}) / (1 + 50); (iv) batch leakage — Kruskal–Wallis of day across run_date / animal-multiplex / region.

Confound controls — sex & region

The panel has Xist but no Y-genes, so sex is called from Xist bimodality (high = female) and tested against day with Mann–Whitney and point-biserial correlation. Region (L/T/C, caudal→rostral) is tested with Kruskal–Wallis and an ordinal L<T<C Spearman against both day and score. The fully-controlled clock re-runs Clock B with covar = [score, sex, region one-hot] and Xist dropped from the features. Source: scripts/duration_clock_controls.py.

Gene-level day decomposition (partial correlation)

For each gene, two partial correlations over the 33 animals: r(gene, day | score) — the accrual axis — and r(gene, score | day) — the oscillation axis — via rxy·z = (rxy − rxzryz) / √((1−rxz²)(1−ryz²)). Significance from t = r√(df/(1−r²)), df = n − 3, with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR across all 5101 genes. Genes are called accruing/declining at |r(day|score)| ≥ 0.30 and severity-oscillating at |r(score|day)| ≥ 0.30 with |r(day|score)| < 0.30. Source: scripts/duration_gene_decomposition.py.

Relapse-cycle oscillation (model-free, stage-stratified)

Within the relapse cycle CFA→ONSET1/2→PEAK1→REM1→PEAK2→REM2→PEAK3, per gene: amplitude = mean(peak animals) − mean(remission animals); floor_drift = mean(REMISSION2) − mean(REMISSION1); peak_drift = PEAK3 − PEAK1; mono_rho = Spearman vs cycle rank. Mann–Whitney (peaks vs remissions) with BH-FDR. Acute oscillating = amplitude > 0.3 with floor_drift < 0.15 (resets); ratchet = floor_drift > 0.2 (survives remission). Source: scripts/rr_cycle_oscillation.py.

Compositional vs cell-intrinsic accrual (shift-share)

25 leiden clusters are collapsed to 10 labelled cell types. Writing pseudobulk as pb(a) = Σc f(a,c)·e(a,c) with cell-type fraction f and per-cell-type mean e, the Oaxaca/shift-share identity splits each animal's deviation into intrinsic Σf̄·δe, compositional Σē·δf, and interaction Σδf·δe. Because covariance is linear, the severity-removed day trend decomposes exactly: Cov(pb, day | score) = Covintr + Covcomp + Covinter (day residualized on score). Per-gene shares are reported over genes that accrue (r(day|score) ≥ 0.30 for the median; ≥ 0.40 for per-gene classification, where shares are stable). Cell-type fraction trends are partial correlations r(fraction, day | score). Source: scripts/duration_composition_intrinsic.py.

Spatial localization (Tier 2)

The severity-orthogonalized Clock B is rebuilt independently inside each cell type and each CellCharter niche from the cached aggregates (leaner: l1-ratio 0.5, 3-fold CV, 30-alpha path, top-800 variance; an animal needs ≥20 cells in a compartment, a compartment ≥30 usable animals). A composition clock predicts day from cell-type fractions alone. Permutation nulls (50×) on the best cell type, best niche, and the composition clock. Source: scripts/duration_clock_spatial.py.

Cross-model replication (chronic arm)

The identical Clock A/B pipeline and the gene-level day decomposition are run on the chronic pseudobulk (runs/chronic_trajectory/pseudobulk.npz) with day/score from the corrected metadata. Because RR (SJL/PLP) and chronic (B6/MOG) differ in strain and slide, only within-model slopes are compared (per-gene day|score partial correlations), which cancels the cross-strain level offset: Spearman of the RR vs chronic day-axis over all 5101 genes, with the RR severity-oscillation axis as a negative-control contrast. Source: scripts/duration_clock_chronic.py.

Honest limits

Both cohorts are small (RR n = 33, chronic n = 34) animal-level pseudobulk (spatial information collapsed) — LOAO + permutation null guard against over-fit but the cohorts are small. The RR sex cohort is imbalanced (7 vs 26) though orthogonal to day. The clock is a supervised regression onto a de-confounded temporal label, not a within-animal time course — there are no per-animal sequences in terminal cross-sectional data. The RR↔chronic comparison is of within-model gene slopes (the cross-strain level offset is not identifiable); chronic day is clean of batch but the chronic cohort still spans two run_dates, controlled only by their both carrying the full day range.

Next

The localization shows the clock is glia-led and state-driven, but the compartment clocks still aggregate each cell type to one number per animal. The finer follow-ups: (1) a within-lesion version using the radial core→rim→margin zones (does duration concentrate in the scar core?); (2) validation in the chronic arm with matched-batch sampling to break the day~run_date confound; (3) a publication-grade null (N_PERM≈1000) on the headline clock.
